title: Fleet scorecard
description: Is the fleet beating a pro team: merged per day, run failure share, idle runner minutes, head to verdict and approval to merge, 14 days.

options.content:
Fleet-ops#10711. Four tables: merged per day, failed share of agent runs, idle agent-runner minutes while ready work waits, and the two at the bottom, head to review verdict and approval to merge (Fleet-ops#10887). The idle table counts runner-minutes with no agent run in flight, on days when an open `agent-ready` issue was waiting, against that day's mean count of online agent runners.

The two tables above bucket days with SUBSTRING, which the expression engine allows, and the merged table searches each repository on its own (Fleet-ops#10853). The failed share counts every non-success finished run, not only infra failures. The verdict and approval tables pair each merged fleet-ops PR with its reviews: the export carries no head commit timestamp, so the head clock starts at the PR opening or at the push that dismissed the previous approval, whichever is later.

No data source yet (fleet-ops#10966): Claude limit per merged PR. Five of the six numbers have a rule in `config/grafana/provisioning/alerting/fleet-scorecard.yaml`, and each files a fleet-ops issue when it misses its target two days running. Targets: idle 0 min/day, verdict p50 < 20 min and p90 < 60 min, infra failures < 2%, approval to merge < 15 min, products ahead of fleet-ops, Claude limit per PR cut 30%.

panels.title: Merged per day, products versus fleet-ops, last 14 days
panels.description: Target: products ahead of fleet-ops. Alert: scorecard-products-behind.

targets.expression:
SELECT d AS day, SUM(CASE WHEN plane = 'products' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS products, SUM(CASE WHEN plane = 'fleet-ops' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fleet_ops
FROM (SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10) AS d, 'fleet-ops' AS plane FROM A UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM B UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM C UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM D UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM E UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM F UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM G UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM H UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(closed_at, 1, 10), 'products' FROM I) AS merged
GROUP BY d ORDER BY d

panels.title: Failed share of agent runs per day, last 14 days
panels.description: agent.yml and agent-dispatch.yml in fleet-ops, finished runs. Target: under 2%. Alert: scorecard-run-failure-share.

targets.expression:
SELECT d AS day, COUNT(*) AS runs, SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion = 'success' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS failed,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN conclusion = 'success' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS failed_percent
FROM (SELECT SUBSTRING(created_at, 1, 10) AS d, conclusion FROM A UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(created_at, 1, 10), conclusion FROM B) AS runs
WHERE conclusion IN ('success', 'failure', 'timed_out', 'startup_failure')
GROUP BY d ORDER BY d

panels.title: Idle agent-runner minutes while ready work waits, per day, last 14 days
panels.description: Target: 0. Runner-minutes on the agent pool with no agent run in flight, on days when an open agent-ready issue was waiting that is not blocked, parked or waiting on a decision. The runner count is the day's mean over online runners. A run's minutes are its own span, booked on the day it started and counted to now while it still runs. Days are UTC. The issue search reads 30 days of issues updated in that window and reads today's labels, so a long-silent wait falls outside it. An empty table means the runner metric is missing.

targets.expression:
WITH days AS (
  SELECT FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP() / 86400) * 86400 - 86400 * n AS day_start,
         CASE WHEN n = 0 THEN (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP() / 86400) * 86400) / 60.0 ELSE 1440 END AS minutes
  FROM (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 3 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 4 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 5 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 6 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 7 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 8 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 9 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 10 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 11 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 12 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 13 AS n) AS spine
), inflight AS (
  SELECT UNIX_TIMESTAMP(run_started_at) AS started,
         CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP(updated_at) ELSE UNIX_TIMESTAMP() END AS ended
  FROM (SELECT run_started_at, status, updated_at FROM A
        UNION ALL SELECT run_started_at, status, updated_at FROM D) AS runs
  WHERE run_started_at IS NOT NULL
), busy AS (
  SELECT FLOOR(started / 86400) AS day_index, SUM(CASE WHEN ended > started THEN ended - started ELSE 0 END) / 60.0 AS busy_minutes
  FROM inflight
  GROUP BY FLOOR(started / 86400)
), slots AS (
  SELECT FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(time) / 86400) AS day_index, AVG(__value__) AS slots FROM P GROUP BY FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(time) / 86400)
), pool AS (SELECT AVG(__value__) AS slots FROM P), waiting AS (
  SELECT d.day_start AS day_start, COUNT(*) AS ready_issues
  FROM days d JOIN B ON UNIX_TIMESTAMP(B.created_at) < d.day_start + 86400 AND COALESCE(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(B.closed_at), UNIX_TIMESTAMP()) >= d.day_start
  GROUP BY d.day_start
)
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(d.day_start), '%Y-%m-%d') AS day,
       COALESCE(w.ready_issues, 0) AS ready_issues,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(w.ready_issues, 0) = 0 THEN 0
            WHEN COALESCE(sl.slots, pool.slots) * d.minutes - COALESCE(bs.busy_minutes, 0) < 0 THEN 0
            ELSE ROUND(COALESCE(sl.slots, pool.slots) * d.minutes - COALESCE(bs.busy_minutes, 0), 0) END AS idle_minutes
FROM days d
CROSS JOIN pool
LEFT JOIN busy bs ON bs.day_index = FLOOR(d.day_start / 86400)
LEFT JOIN slots sl ON sl.day_index = FLOOR(d.day_start / 86400)
LEFT JOIN waiting w ON w.day_start = d.day_start
ORDER BY d.day_start

panels.title: Head to review verdict, p50 and p90 minutes per day, last 14 days
panels.description: Target: p50 under 20 min, p90 under 60 min. One row per merged fleet-ops PR, on the day it merged: from the newest head the GitHub export can date to the APPROVED verdict that merged it. Days are UTC. The verdict is the last APPROVED review at or before merged_at, so a verdict that arrives after the merge does not count. The head is the PR opening, or the push that dismissed the previous approval when that is later. The export carries no head commit timestamp, so a push that lands while no approval is live is folded into the wait and a PR pushed repeatedly between verdicts shows the whole rework wait. A PR merged without an APPROVED review is absent.

targets.expression:
WITH pair AS (
  SELECT a.number AS pr,
         MIN(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.created_at)) AS opened_at,
         MIN(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.merged_at)) AS merged_at,
         MAX(CASE WHEN b.review_state = 'APPROVED' AND UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_created_at) <= UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.merged_at) THEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_created_at) END) AS verdict_at,
         MAX(CASE WHEN b.review_state = 'DISMISSED' AND UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_updated_at) <= UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.merged_at) THEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_updated_at) END) AS dismissed_at
  FROM A AS a JOIN B AS b ON b.pull_request_number = a.number
  GROUP BY a.number
), minutes AS (
  SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(merged_at), '%Y-%m-%d') AS day,
         (verdict_at - CASE WHEN dismissed_at > opened_at AND dismissed_at < verdict_at THEN dismissed_at ELSE opened_at END) / 60.0 AS waiting
  FROM pair WHERE verdict_at IS NOT NULL
), ranked AS (
  SELECT day, waiting,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY day ORDER BY waiting) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY day) AS c
  FROM minutes
)
SELECT day, COUNT(*) AS prs,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rn >= (c + 1) / 2.0 - 0.5 AND rn <= (c + 1) / 2.0 + 0.5 THEN waiting END), 1) AS p50_minutes,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.9 * c) THEN waiting END), 1) AS p90_minutes
FROM ranked GROUP BY day ORDER BY day

panels.title: Approval to merge, p50 and p90 minutes per day, last 14 days
panels.description: Target: under 15 min. One row per merged fleet-ops PR, on the day it merged: from the APPROVED verdict that armed the merge to merged_at. Days are UTC. The verdict is the last APPROVED review at or before merged_at, so a PR merged without an APPROVED review is absent.

targets.expression:
WITH pair AS (
  SELECT a.number AS pr,
         MIN(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.created_at)) AS opened_at,
         MIN(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.merged_at)) AS merged_at,
         MAX(CASE WHEN b.review_state = 'APPROVED' AND UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_created_at) <= UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.merged_at) THEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_created_at) END) AS verdict_at,
         MAX(CASE WHEN b.review_state = 'DISMISSED' AND UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_updated_at) <= UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.merged_at) THEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP(b.review_updated_at) END) AS dismissed_at
  FROM A AS a JOIN B AS b ON b.pull_request_number = a.number
  GROUP BY a.number
), minutes AS (
  SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(merged_at), '%Y-%m-%d') AS day,
         (merged_at - verdict_at) / 60.0 AS waiting
  FROM pair WHERE verdict_at IS NOT NULL
), ranked AS (
  SELECT day, waiting,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY day ORDER BY waiting) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY day) AS c
  FROM minutes
)
SELECT day, COUNT(*) AS prs,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rn >= (c + 1) / 2.0 - 0.5 AND rn <= (c + 1) / 2.0 + 0.5 THEN waiting END), 1) AS p50_minutes,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.9 * c) THEN waiting END), 1) AS p90_minutes
FROM ranked GROUP BY day ORDER BY day
